```{r, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, results='hide', warning=FALSE}
  "stigma_percept_5","stigma_percept_6","stigma_percept_7","stigma_percept_8", "Score_lubben", "score_PHQ9", "DIAG_NOW_3_Age", "nb_maladies_psy", "nb_maladies_somatiques", "nb_PEC1", "nb_PEC2","Score_BIPQ", "Score_whodas", "score_GAD7", "Score_autostigma"

to_num <- function(x) {
  x <- trimws(as.character(x))
  x <- gsub(",", ".", x, fixed = TRUE)
  suppressWarnings(as.numeric(x))
}

dat[num_vars] <- lapply(dat[num_vars], to_num)
```

# S3. Internal consistency {.tabset}

## B-IPQ

### Items Distribution

```{r, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE }

# Garder uniquement les items B-IPQ
items <- c("item 1", "item 2", "item 3", "item 4",
           "item 5", "item 6", "item 7", "item 8")

data_efa <- dat[, c(items)]

vars <- paste0("item ", 1:8)

d <- descr(
  data_efa[vars],
  stats = c("skewness", "kurtosis"),
  transpose = TRUE
)

# Convertit l'objet summarytools en data.frame exploitable
tab <- as.data.frame(d)

# Les colonnes s'appellent généralement "Skewness" / "Kurtosis" (casse variable selon versions)

skew_kurt_table <- data.frame(
  variable = rownames(tab),
  skewness = as.numeric(tab[[grep("skew", names(tab), ignore.case = TRUE, value = TRUE)[1]]]),
  kurtosis = as.numeric(tab[[grep("kurt", names(tab), ignore.case = TRUE, value = TRUE)[1]]]),
  row.names = NULL
)

skew_kurt_table$skewness <- round(skew_kurt_table$skewness, 2)
skew_kurt_table$kurtosis <- round(skew_kurt_table$kurtosis, 2)


# -----------------------------
# 2) Data-visualisation globale avec dfSummary (mini histogrammes + NA, etc.)
# -----------------------------
dfs <- dfSummary(
  data_efa[vars],
  style      = "grid",
  graph.col  = TRUE,   # mini-graphiques dans la colonne Graph
  valid.col  = TRUE,
  na.col     = TRUE
)


# ou rendu console / HTML
print(dfs, method = "render")


```

### Skewness and kurtosis
```{r, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE }

# affichage skewness and kurtosis
skew_kurt_table%>%
  kbl() %>%
  kable_styling()%>%
  column_spec(1, bold = TRUE)
```



### ICC

```{r, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
items <- data_efa[, c("item 1", "item 2", "item 3", "item 4",
           "item 5", "item 6", "item 7", "item 8")]


# Compute the Spearman correlation matrix
iic <- cor(items, method = "spearman", use = "pairwise.complete.obs")
round(iic, 2)  %>%
  kbl() %>%
  kable_styling()%>%
  column_spec(1, bold = TRUE)



# Heatmap 
corrplot(iic, method = "color", type = "upper",
         addCoef.col = "black", # ajoute les valeurs
         tl.col = "black", tl.srt = 45,
         diag = FALSE)

```

### ITC

```{r, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE,  warning=FALSE}
items <- data_efa[vars]

# Cronbach alpha
alpha_result <- psych::alpha(items, check.keys = FALSE)


# Corrected item-total correlations (r.drop)
r_drop <- alpha_result$item.stats$r.drop
names(r_drop) <- colnames(items)

alpha_table <- data.frame(
  item = rownames(alpha_result$item.stats),
  mean = alpha_result$item.stats$mean,
  sd   = alpha_result$item.stats$sd,
  r_drop = alpha_result$item.stats$r.drop,
  alpha_if_deleted = alpha_result$alpha.drop$raw_alpha,
  row.names = NULL
)

alpha_table%>%
  kbl() %>%
  kable_styling()%>%
  column_spec(1, bold = TRUE)

```





### Floor ceiling

```{r,echo=FALSE, message=FALSE,  warning=FALSE}

# items = data.frame d'items numériques
floor_ceiling <- t(sapply(items, function(x) {
  x <- x[is.finite(x)]
  n <- length(x)
  if (n == 0) return(c(Floor = NA_real_, Ceiling = NA_real_))

  floor_effect   <- sum(x == min(x)) / n * 100
  ceiling_effect <- sum(x == max(x)) / n * 100

  c(Floor = round(floor_effect, 1), Ceiling = round(ceiling_effect, 1))
}))

floor_ceiling <- as.data.frame(floor_ceiling)
floor_ceiling$item <- rownames(floor_ceiling)
rownames(floor_ceiling) <- NULL



stats <- data.frame(
  item = names(items),
  n    = sapply(items, function(x) sum(is.finite(x))),
  min  = sapply(items, function(x) min(x, na.rm = TRUE)),
  max  = sapply(items, function(x) max(x, na.rm = TRUE)),
  mean = sapply(items, function(x) mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)),
  sd   = sapply(items, function(x) sd(x, na.rm = TRUE))
)

report_tbl <- stats %>%
  left_join(floor_ceiling, by = "item") %>%
  mutate(
    mean = round(mean, 2),
    sd   = round(sd, 2)
  )

report_tbl %>%
  kbl(caption = "Item-level descriptive statistics and floor/ceiling effects of the B-IPQ") %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE) %>%
  column_spec(1, bold = TRUE)


```

```{r,echo=FALSE, message=FALSE,  warning=FALSE}
# items = data.frame d'items numériques
```

# S4. Structural validity {.tabset}

## B-IPQ
### unidimensional CFA

```{r, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE,  warning=FALSE}
data_efa_bipq <- data_efa %>%
  rename(
    item1 = `item 1`,
    item2 = `item 2`,
    item3 = `item 3`,
    item4 = `item 4`,
    item5 = `item 5`,
    item6 = `item 6`,
    item7 = `item 7`,
    item8 = `item 8`
  )
```


```{r}
items_bipq <- paste0("item", 1:8)
cfa_model <- '
BIPQ =~ item1 + item2 + item3 + item4 +
        item5 + item6 + item7 + item8
'
fit_bipq_1f <- cfa(
  cfa_model,
  data = data_efa_bipq,
  estimator = "WLSMV",
  ordered = items_bipq
)
summary(fit_bipq_1f, fit.measures = TRUE, standardized = TRUE, rsquare = TRUE)
# Robust fit indices
fitMeasures(
  fit_bipq_1f,
  c(
    "cfi.robust",
    "rmsea.robust",
    "rmsea.ci.lower.robust",
    "rmsea.ci.upper.robust",
    "srmr"
  )
)

```

```{r, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE,  warning=FALSE}

library(semPlot)

semPaths(
  fit_bipq_1f,
  what = "std",
  whatLabels = "std",
  layout = "tree",
  style = "lisrel",
  rotation = 2,

  # Masquer les paramètres supplémentaires
  residuals = FALSE,
  intercepts = FALSE,
  thresholds = FALSE,

  # Affichage des variables
  nCharNodes = 0,
  sizeMan = 7,
  sizeLat = 10,

  # Affichage des coefficients
  edge.label.cex = 1,
  label.cex = 1,

  # Apparence
  color = "white",
  edge.color = "black",
  fade = FALSE,
  mar = c(5, 5, 5, 5)
)


```


Sensibility analysis with "MLR"
```{r}

cfa_model <- '
BIPQ =~ item1 + item2 + item3 + item4 +
        item5 + item6 + item7 + item8
'
fit_bipq_1fmlr <- cfa(
  cfa_model,
  data = data_efa_bipq,
  estimator = "MLR"
)
summary(fit_bipq_1fmlr, fit.measures = TRUE, standardized = TRUE, rsquare = TRUE)
# Robust fit indices
fitMeasures(
  fit_bipq_1fmlr,
  c(
    "cfi.robust",
    "rmsea.robust",
    "rmsea.ci.lower.robust",
    "rmsea.ci.upper.robust",
    "srmr"
  )
)

```


### CFA comparison

The weak contribution of items 4 and 7 may reflect participants’ treatment appraisal and illness understanding, possibly linked to care engagement, psychotherapy exposure, repeated depressive episodes, or contact with specialized mental health care, rather than item misinterpretation.

```{r, warning=FALSE}

# alternative model 1

cfa_model_multi <- '
F1 =~ item1 + item5 + item6 + item8
F2 =~ item3 + item4 + item7
'

fit_multi_bipq1 <- cfa(
  cfa_model_multi,
  data = data_efa_bipq,
  estimator = "WLSMV",
  ordered = paste0("item", c(1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8))
)

summary(
  fit_multi_bipq1,
  fit.measures = TRUE,
  standardized = TRUE,
  rsquare = TRUE
)

# Robust fit indices
fitMeasures(
  fit_multi_bipq1,
  c(
    "cfi.robust",
    "rmsea.robust",
    "rmsea.ci.lower.robust",
    "rmsea.ci.upper.robust",
    "srmr"
  )
)
```
```{r, warning=FALSE}

# alternative model 2

cfa_model_multi_2 <- '
F1 =~ item1 + item2 + item5 + item6 + item8
F2 =~ item3 + item4 + item7
'

fit_multi_bipq2 <- cfa(
  cfa_model_multi_2,
  data = data_efa_bipq,
  estimator = "WLSMV",
  ordered = paste0("item", 1:8)
)

summary(
  fit_multi_bipq2,
  fit.measures = TRUE,
  standardized = TRUE,
  rsquare = TRUE
)

# Robust fit indices
fitMeasures(
  fit_multi_bipq2,
  c(
    "cfi.robust",
    "rmsea.robust",
    "rmsea.ci.lower.robust",
    "rmsea.ci.upper.robust",
    "srmr"
  )
)
```

Sensitivity analysis with MLR 

```{r, warning=FALSE}

### model 1 

cfa_model_multi <- '
F1 =~ item1 + item5 + item6 + item8
F2 =~ item3 + item4 + item7
# Item 2 was not assigned to any factor and was retained as an independent item.
'
fit_multi_bipqmlr1 <- cfa(cfa_model_multi, data = data_efa_bipq, estimator = "MLR")
summary(fit_multi_bipqmlr1, fit.measures = TRUE, standardized = TRUE, rsquare = TRUE)
# Robust fit indices
fitMeasures(
  fit_multi_bipqmlr1,
  c(
    "cfi.robust",
    "rmsea.robust",
    "rmsea.ci.lower.robust",
    "rmsea.ci.upper.robust",
    "srmr"
  )
)

### model 2 

cfa_model_multi_2 <- '
F1 =~ item1 + item2 + item5 + item6 + item8
F2 =~ item3 + item4 + item7
'
fit_multi_bipqmlr2 <- cfa(cfa_model_multi_2, data = data_efa_bipq, estimator = "MLR")

summary(fit_multi_bipqmlr2, fit.measures = TRUE, standardized = TRUE, rsquare = TRUE)

# Robust fit indices
fitMeasures(
  fit_multi_bipqmlr2,
  c(
    "cfi.robust",
    "rmsea.robust",
    "rmsea.ci.lower.robust",
    "rmsea.ci.upper.robust",
    "srmr"
  )
)
```

Both previously reported two-factor B-IPQ models yielded inadmissible solutions under WLSMV estimation, with negative residual variances for item 3 (−2.416 and −2.789 for the first and second models, respectively) and standardised factor loadings exceeding 1 (1.848 and 1.947, respectively). Sensitivity analyses using MLR yielded the same estimation issue, with negative residual variances for item 3 (−6.754 and −6.962, respectively) and standardised loadings of 1.450 and 1.461, respectively.

Bifactor model
```{r}
# Bifactor model
cfa_model_phq_bifactor <- '
# General factor
General =~ item1 + item2 + item3 + item4 + item5 +
           item6 + item7 + item8 + item9

# Specific factors
Somatic =~ item3 + item4 + item5 + item8

CognitiveAffective =~ item1 + item2 + item6 + item7 + item9

# Orthogonal factors
General ~~ 0*Somatic
General ~~ 0*CognitiveAffective
Somatic ~~ 0*CognitiveAffective
'

fit_phq_bifactor <- cfa(
  cfa_model_phq_bifactor,
  data = data_efa_phq,
  estimator = "WLSMV",
  ordered = items_phq,
  std.lv = TRUE
)

# Model summary
summary(
  fit_phq_bifactor,
  fit.measures = TRUE,
  standardized = TRUE,
  rsquare = TRUE
)

# Robust fit indices
fitMeasures(
  fit_phq_bifactor,
  c(
    "cfi.robust",
    "tli.robust",
    "rmsea.robust",
    "rmsea.ci.lower.robust",
    "rmsea.ci.upper.robust",
    "srmr"
  )
)
```



```{r}

# Extract robust fit indices
indices <- c(
  "cfi.robust",
  "rmsea.robust",
  "rmsea.ci.lower.robust",
  "rmsea.ci.upper.robust",
  "srmr"
)

# Comparison table
comparison_phq <- rbind(
  Unidimensional = fitMeasures(fit_phq_1f, indices),
  Two_factor = fitMeasures(fit_phq_2f, indices),
  Bifactor = fitMeasures(fit_phq_bifactor, indices)
)

round(comparison_phq, 3)

```

Supplementary bifactorial indices

```{r}
# 1. Extraire les saturations factorielles standardisées
L <- inspect(fit_phq_bifactor, "std")$lambda

# Vérifier la structure
print(L)

# 2. Extraire les variances résiduelles standardisées
theta <- diag(inspect(fit_phq_bifactor, "std")$theta)

# 3. Saturations sur les trois facteurs
g <- L[, "General"]
s <- L[, "Somatic"]
c <- L[, "CognitiveAffective"]

# 4. Explained Common Variance (ECV)
ECV <- sum(g^2) / sum(L^2)

# 5. Omega total (omega)
variance_totale_commune <- sum(colSums(L)^2)
variance_erreur <- sum(theta)

omega <- variance_totale_commune /
  (variance_totale_commune + variance_erreur)

# 6. Omega hiérarchique (omega H)
omegaH <- sum(g)^2 /
  (variance_totale_commune + variance_erreur)

# 7. Afficher les résultats
data.frame(
  Index = c("Omega total", "Omega hierarchical", "ECV"),
  Value = round(c(omega, omegaH, ECV), 3)
)

```

```{r}

cfa_model_sss_bifactor <- '
# General factor
General =~ item1 + item2 + item3 + item4 + item5 +
           item6 + item7 + item8 + item9

# Specific factors
  Cognitive =~ item1 + item2 + item3
  Affective =~ item4 + item5 + item6
  Behavioural =~ item7 + item8 + item9

 # Orthogonality between general and specific factors
  General ~~ 0*Cognitive
  General ~~ 0*Affective
  General ~~ 0*Behavioural

  # Orthogonality between specific factors
  Cognitive ~~ 0*Affective
  Cognitive ~~ 0*Behavioural
  Affective ~~ 0*Behavioural
'
```

```{r}
  pe$op == "~~" &

]


pe[
  pe$lhs == "ExternalStigma" &
  pe$op == "=~",

]
```

# S5. Exploratory hypothesis testing {.tabset}

## Convergent validity

### Simple correlation

```{r, warning=FALSE}

dat_bis <- dat %>%
  dplyr::select(score_PHQ9, Score_autostigma, Score_BIPQ, Score_whodas, score_GAD7)

cor_spearman2 <- cor(dat_bis$Score_BIPQ, dat_bis$score_PHQ9, method = "spearman", use = "complete.obs")
cor.test(dat_bis$Score_BIPQ, dat_bis$score_PHQ9, method = "spearman")

cor_spearman3 <- cor(dat_bis$Score_BIPQ, dat_bis$score_GAD7, method = "spearman", use = "complete.obs")

cor.test(dat_bis$Score_BIPQ, dat_bis$score_GAD7, method = "spearman")


```

### Latent model

### BIPQ \~ PHQ9

####  Freely estimated latent correlations

```{r,  echo=FALSE, message=FALSE,  warning=FALSE}

dat <- dat %>%
  rename(
    item1 = `item 1`,
    item2 = `item 2`,
    item3 = `item 3`,
    item4 = `item 4`,
    item5 = `item 5`,
    item6 = `item 6`,
    item7 = `item 7`,
    item8 = `item 8`
  )

var_phq <- c("id_unik", "score_PHQ9", "interet_plaisir",	"triste_deprime",	"sommeil",	"fatigue",	"appetit",	"opinion_soi",	"concentration",	"activite",	"consequence_pb",
             
             "Score_BIPQ", "item1", "item2", "item3", "item4","item5", "item6", "item7", "item8"
)
data_phq <-dat[, c(var_phq)]
```


```{r, warning=FALSE}


cfa_model_PHQ <- '
BIPQ =~ item1 + item5 + item6 + item8 + item3 + item4 + item7 + item2
PHQ9 =~ interet_plaisir + triste_deprime + sommeil + fatigue + appetit + opinion_soi + concentration + activite + consequence_pb
BIPQ ~~ PHQ9'

fit_PHQ <- cfa(cfa_model_PHQ, 
               data = data_phq, 
               estimator = "MLR", 
               std.lv = TRUE,
               missing   = "fiml")

#summary(fit_PHQ, fit.measures = TRUE, standardized = TRUE, rsquare = TRUE)
fitMeasures(fit_PHQ, c("cfi", "tli", "rmsea", "srmr"))


# 95% confidence interval for the latent variable correlation
latcorPHQ <- parameterEstimates(fit_PHQ, standardized = TRUE, ci = TRUE)

# Result of interest
subset(latcorPHQ, lhs == "BIPQ" & rhs == "PHQ9" & op == "~~")[, 
        c("est", "ci.lower", "ci.upper", "pvalue")]

```

#### Constrained two-factor models (correlation == 0.9)

```{r, warning=FALSE}
cfa_PHQ_corr <- '
BIPQ =~ item1 + item5 + item6 + item8 + item3 + item4 + item7 + item2
PHQ9 =~ interet_plaisir + triste_deprime + sommeil + fatigue + appetit + opinion_soi + concentration + activite + consequence_pb
BIPQ ~~ 0.9*PHQ9
'
fit_PHQ_corr <- cfa(cfa_PHQ_corr,
                    data = data_phq,
                    estimator = "MLR", 
                    std.lv = TRUE,
                    missing   = "fiml")

#summary(fit_PHQ_corr, fit.measures = TRUE, standardized = TRUE)
fitMeasures(fit_PHQ_corr, c("cfi", "tli", "rmsea", "srmr"))

```

Comparison using scaled chi-square difference tests with the Satorra–Bentler 2010 correction.
 
```{r}
lavTestLRT(
  fit_PHQ,
  fit_PHQ_corr,
  method = "satorra.bentler.2010"
)
```

```{r}
)

#summary(fit_GAD, fit.measures = TRUE, standardized = TRUE, rsquare = TRUE)
fitMeasures(fit_GAD, c("cfi", "tli", "rmsea", "srmr"))

# 95% confidence interval for the latent variable correlation
latcorGAD <- parameterEstimates(fit_GAD, standardized = TRUE, ci = TRUE)

# Result of interest
subset(latcorGAD, lhs == "BIPQ" & rhs == "GAD7" & op == "~~")[, 
       c("est", "ci.lower", "ci.upper", "pvalue")]

```



#### Constrained two-factor models (correlation == 0.9)

```{r}
cfa_GAD_corr <- '
BIPQ =~ item1 + item5 + item6 + item8 + item3 + item4 + item7 + item2
GAD7 =~ nerveux + inquiet + inquiet_exces + difficult_detente + agitation + tendance_contrarie + sentiment_peur
BIPQ ~~ 0.9*GAD7
'

fit_GAD_corr <- cfa(cfa_GAD_corr, 
                    data = data_gad,
                    estimator = "MLR",
                    std.lv = TRUE,
                    missing = "fiml" 
)

#summary(fit_GAD_corr, fit.measures = TRUE, standardized = TRUE)
fitMeasures(fit_GAD_corr, c("cfi", "tli", "rmsea", "srmr"))

```

Comparison using scaled chi-square difference tests with the Satorra–Bentler 2010 correction.

```{r}
lavTestLRT(
  fit_GAD,
  fit_GAD_corr,
  method = "satorra.bentler.2010"
)
```

## With anova

```{r}
dat_bis <- dat %>%
  dplyr::select(
    age, Sexe, score_PHQ9, Score_autostigma,
    Score_BIPQ, Score_whodas, score_GAD7
  )

dat_clean <- dat_bis[complete.cases(dat_bis), ]

r2 <- function(m) summary(m)$r.squared

model1 <- lm(
  Score_whodas ~ age + Sexe,
  data = dat_clean
)

model2 <- lm(
  Score_whodas ~ age + Sexe + score_PHQ9 + Score_autostigma + score_GAD7,
  data = dat_clean
)

model3 <- lm(
  Score_whodas ~ age + Sexe + score_PHQ9 + Score_autostigma + score_GAD7 + Score_BIPQ,
  data = dat_clean
)

# ANOVA hiérarchique
anova_results <- anova(model1, model2, model3)

print(anova_results)
```

```{r, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE,  warning=FALSE}

dat_bis <- dat %>%
  dplyr::select(age, Sexe, score_PHQ9, Score_autostigma, Score_BIPQ, Score_whodas, score_GAD7)

## Commonality analysis 
dat_clean <- dat_bis[complete.cases(dat_bis[, c("Score_whodas",
                                             "score_PHQ9",
                                             "Score_autostigma",
                                             "score_GAD7",
                                             "Score_BIPQ")]), ]

r2 <- function(m) summary(m)$r.squared

model1 <- lm(
  Score_whodas ~ age + Sexe,
  data = dat_clean
)

model2 <- lm(
  Score_whodas ~ age + Sexe + score_PHQ9 + Score_autostigma + score_GAD7,
  data = dat_clean
)

model3 <- lm(
  Score_whodas ~ age + Sexe + score_PHQ9 + Score_autostigma + score_GAD7 + Score_BIPQ,
  data = dat_clean
)

r2_1 <- r2(model1)
r2_2 <- r2(model2)
r2_3 <- r2(model3)

r2_table <- data.frame(
  Model = c("Step 1: age + sex",
            "Step 2: + PHQ-9 + SSS-S + GAD-7",
            "Step 3: + BIPQ"),
  R2 = c(r2(model1), r2(model2), r2(model3))
)

r2_table$Delta_R2 <- c(NA, diff(r2_table$R2))

r2_table$R2_percent <- round(r2_table$R2 * 100, 2)
r2_table$Delta_R2_percent <- round(r2_table$Delta_R2 * 100, 2)

r2_table

# Ordre des composants
order_blocks <- c(
  "Age + sex",
  "PHQ-9 + SSS-S + GAD-7",
  "BIPQ",
  "Unexplained"
)

fill_blocks <- c(
  "Age + sex"                    = "#3A67A4",
  "PHQ-9 + SSS-S + GAD-7"  = "#B2A5D1",
  "BIPQ"                         = "#29A274",
  "Unexplained"                  = "#E9E7E1"
)

# Table des incréments
block_table <- tibble(
  Component = c(
    "Age + sex",
    "PHQ-9 + SSS-S + GAD-7",
    "BIPQ",
    "Unexplained"
  ),
  Value = c(
    r2_1,
    r2_2 - r2_1,
    r2_3 - r2_2,
    1 - r2_3
  )
) %>%
  mutate(
    Percent = Value * 100,
    Label = sprintf("%.2f%%", Percent),
    Component = factor(Component, levels = order_blocks)
  ) %>%
  arrange(Component) %>%
  mutate(
    xmin = lag(cumsum(Percent), default = 0),
    xmax = cumsum(Percent),
    xmid = (xmin + xmax) / 2,
    
    # Label BIPQ placé au-dessus car segment trop petit
    label_x = ifelse(Component == "BIPQ", xmax + 3, xmid),
    label_y = ifelse(Component == "BIPQ", 1.32, 1)
  )


ggplot(block_table) +
  geom_rect(
    aes(
      xmin = xmin,
      xmax = xmax,
      ymin = 0.8,
      ymax = 1.2,
      fill = Component
    )
  ) +
  geom_text(
    aes(
      x = label_x,
      y = label_y,
      label = Label
    ),
    size = 3.3
  ) +
  geom_segment(
    data = block_table %>% filter(Component == "BIPQ"),
    aes(
      x = xmid,
      xend = label_x,
      y = 1.18,
      yend = 1.27
    ),
    linewidth = 0.3
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = fill_blocks,
    breaks = order_blocks[order_blocks != "Unexplained"],
    name = NULL
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq(0, 100, 10),
    labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%"),
    limits = c(0, 105),
    expand = c(0, 0)
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Percentage of WHODAS-12 variance",
    y = NULL,
    title = sprintf("WHODAS-12 — hierarchical explained variance, total R² = %.2f%%", r2_3 * 100)
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.title = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    axis.text.y = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.y = element_blank()
  )
```

```{r, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE,  warning=FALSE}
# =========================
# 1. Calcul des variances uniques
# =========================

r2 <- function(m) summary(m)$r.squared

model_full <- lm(
  Score_whodas ~ age + Sexe + score_PHQ9 + Score_autostigma + score_GAD7 + Score_BIPQ,
  data = dat_clean
)

r2_full <- r2(model_full)

unique_table_block <- tibble(
  Predictor = c(
    "Age + sex",
    "PHQ-9",
    "Self-stigma",
    "GAD-7",
    "BIPQ"
  ),
  Unique_R2 = c(
    # Age + sex retirés ensemble
    r2_full - r2(lm(
      Score_whodas ~ score_PHQ9 + Score_autostigma + score_GAD7 + Score_BIPQ,
      data = dat_clean
    )),
    
    # PHQ-9 retiré
    r2_full - r2(lm(
      Score_whodas ~ age + Sexe + Score_autostigma + score_GAD7 + Score_BIPQ,
      data = dat_clean
    )),
    
    # Self-stigma retiré
    r2_full - r2(lm(
      Score_whodas ~ age + Sexe + score_PHQ9 + score_GAD7 + Score_BIPQ,
      data = dat_clean
    )),
    
    # GAD-7 retiré
    r2_full - r2(lm(
      Score_whodas ~ age + Sexe + score_PHQ9 + Score_autostigma + Score_BIPQ,
      data = dat_clean
    )),
    
    # BIPQ retiré
    r2_full - r2(lm(
      Score_whodas ~ age + Sexe + score_PHQ9 + Score_autostigma + score_GAD7,
      data = dat_clean
    ))
  )
) %>%
  mutate(
    Percent = Unique_R2 * 100,
    Label = sprintf("%.2f%%", Percent)
  )

# =========================
# 2. Préparation du graphique
# =========================

unique_plot <- unique_table_block %>%
  transmute(
    Component = Predictor,
    Percent = Percent
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Component = recode(Component, "Self-stigma" = "SSS-S")
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(Percent)) %>%
  mutate(
    Component = factor(Component, levels = Component),
    Label = sprintf("%.2f%%", Percent),
    
    xmin = lag(cumsum(Percent), default = 0),
    xmax = cumsum(Percent),
    xmid = (xmin + xmax) / 2,
    
    label_text = case_when(
      Component == "SSS-S" ~ paste0("SSS-S: ", Label),
      Component == "BIPQ"  ~ paste0("BIPQ: ", Label),
      TRUE ~ Label
    ),
    
    label_x = case_when(
      Component == "SSS-S" ~ xmid,
      Component == "BIPQ"  ~ xmax + 0.75,
      TRUE ~ xmid
    ),
    
    label_y = case_when(
      Component == "SSS-S" ~ 1.55,
      Component == "BIPQ"  ~ 1.00,
      TRUE ~ 1.00
    ),
    
    hjust_label = case_when(
      Component == "BIPQ" ~ 0,
      TRUE ~ 0.5
    )
  )

# =========================
# 3. Graphique
# =========================

fill_unique <- c(
  "PHQ-9"     = "#3A67A4",
  "GAD-7"     = "#60CDA0",
  "Age + sex" = "#B2A5D1",
  "SSS-S"     = "#E68613",
  "BIPQ"      = "#7B2CBF"
)

ggplot(unique_plot) +
  geom_rect(
    aes(
      xmin = xmin,
      xmax = xmax,
      ymin = 0.8,
      ymax = 1.2,
      fill = Component
    )
  ) +
  
  geom_text(
    aes(
      x = label_x,
      y = label_y,
      label = label_text,
      hjust = hjust_label
    ),
    size = 3.3
  ) +
  
  # Trait vertical pour SSS-S
  geom_segment(
    data = unique_plot %>% filter(Component == "SSS-S"),
    aes(
      x = xmid,
      xend = xmid,
      y = 1.2,
      yend = 1.45
    ),
    linewidth = 0.3
  ) +
  
  # Trait horizontal pour BIPQ
  geom_segment(
    data = unique_plot %>% filter(Component == "BIPQ"),
    aes(
      x = xmax,
      xend = label_x - 0.15,
      y = 1.0,
      yend = 1.0
    ),
    linewidth = 0.3
  ) +
  
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = fill_unique,
    breaks = levels(unique_plot$Component),
    name = NULL,
    guide = guide_legend(nrow = 1, byrow = TRUE)
  ) +
  
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq(0, 14, 1),
    labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%"),
    limits = c(0, 14),
    expand = c(0, 0)
  ) +
  
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0.75, 1.70), clip = "off") +
  
  labs(
    x = "Unique variance explained in WHODAS-12",
    y = NULL,
    title = "WHODAS-12 — unique contributions"
  ) +
  
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.title = element_blank(),
    legend.spacing.x = unit(0.8, "cm"),
    legend.key.width = unit(0.9, "cm"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 9),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    axis.text.y = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.y = element_blank()
  )
```



## with yhat

Commonality analysis

```{r}
# Modèle final
res_lm <- lm(
  Score_whodas ~ age + Sexe + score_PHQ9 + Score_autostigma + score_GAD7 + Score_BIPQ,
  data = dat_clean
)

# Commonality analysis
res_common <- calc.yhat(res_lm)

# Bootstrap 1000 resamples
boot_out <- boot(
  data = dat_clean,
  statistic = yhat::boot.yhat,
  R = 1000,
  lmOut = res_lm,
  regrout0 = res_common
)

# IC 95% percentile
boot_results <- booteval.yhat(
  res_common,
  boot_out,
  bty = "perc",
  .95,
  3
)

# Results
print(res_common$PredictorMetrics)
print(res_common$OrderedPredictorMetrics)
print(res_common$PairedDominanceMetrics)


# Incremental contribution of the BIPQ to WHODAS-12 explained variance
bipq_incremental <- boot_results$combCIaps[
  "age,Sexe,score_PHQ9,Score_autostigma,score_GAD7",
  "Score_BIPQ.Inc"
]

print(bipq_incremental)
```
